analysis.answer: Current law allows demonstrations on public sidewalks subject to general traffic and noise rules. The measure creates a specific 100-foot buffer zone around the entrances of facilities providing abortion services during their operating hours, within which no person may demonstrate.

Patients and staff of abortion facilities benefit from a designated area free of demonstrations. Demonstrators bear the cost of being physically distanced from their target audience, reducing their ability to directly interact with individuals entering the clinic.

Demonstrators will be required to move their activities outside the 100-foot radius, which may lead them to use different tactics, such as larger signs or amplified sound, to convey their message from a distance. Law enforcement agencies will need to delineate and enforce the 100-foot boundaries.

The measure addresses the issue of patients facing confrontation, harassment, or physical obstruction when attempting to enter abortion clinics. The mechanism reaches this by establishing a mandatory physical separation between demonstrators and the clinic entrances.

Researchers disagree on the precise impacts of buffer zones. Some find they successfully reduce patient anxiety, harassment, and clinic vandalism by creating safe physical access. Others argue they severely limit the effectiveness of demonstrators' speech and outreach efforts by removing their ability to engage in quiet, one-on-one conversation or hand out literature near the entrance.
